candidates.relationship: loose image parallel with material and referent differences
candidates.similarity: Wind disperses lightweight material to represent the ultimate futility or fate of wickedness.
candidates.difference: Qur'an: ashes (ramad), storm wind, specifically the deeds of unbelievers and inability to retain what they earned. Psalm: chaff (mots), wind, wicked persons, contrasting righteous and wicked; no ashes or deeds as explicit referent.
candidates.language_checked: Qur'anic Arabic and English at Quran.com; Hebrew Masoretic reading and English JPS 1917 at IsraelFM and Hebrew interlinear at Knowing Jesus
candidates.witnesses_checked: Web-transcribed Masoretic text only; no critical apparatus or ancient manuscript collations
candidates.composition_note: Psalm 1 composition and redaction not established by this pass; extant medieval Masoretic vocalization is not composition date.

historical_dossier.topic: Wind-driven ash and chaff as judgment imagery: Qur'an 14:18 and Psalm 1:4
historical_dossier.discussion: Both use wind to convey loss, but Qur'an speaks of deeds as ash in a violent storm and Psalm 1:4 speaks of wicked people as chaff. The shared image does not establish direct transmission. Further study should include Isaiah 17:13 and Psalm 35:5 as alternative biblical imagery, not yet checked as candidates.
historical_dossier.required: Psalm dating and collection history; Masoretic, LXX, Syriac witnesses; Qur'anic tafsir reception; scholarship on wisdom imagery; bibliographic editions; distinct verses and bidirectional links.
